title: Least Squares & QR Decomposition
description: Linear least-squares problems, normal equations, Gram–Schmidt, Householder and Givens QR.
html:
📐 Least Squares & QR Decomposition

1. Least-Squares Problem and Normal Equations

$$\min_x\|Ax - b\|_2, \quad A \in \mathbb R^{m\times n},\ m > n \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad A^TAx = A^Tb$$

Geometrically: $Ax$ = projection of $b$ onto $\mathrm{range}(A)$; residual $r = b - Ax \perp$ columns of $A$ ($A^Tr = 0$). Unique for full column rank.

Example

Line through $(0,1), (1,2), (2,2), (3,4)$: $A^TA = \begin{pmatrix}4&6\\6&14\end{pmatrix}$, $A^Tb = (9, 18)^T$ ⇒ $c_0 = c_1 = 0.9$, $\|r\|^2 = 0.7$.

Weakness: $\mathrm{cond}_2(A^TA) = \mathrm{cond}_2(A)^2$.

2. QR Decomposition

$$A = QR,\; Q^TQ = I: \qquad \|Ax - b\|_2 = \|Rx - Q^Tb\|_2 \;\Rightarrow\; R_1x = c_1\ (\text{back substitution}),\;\; \|r\|_2 = \|c_2\|_2$$

  • Gram–Schmidt: $r_{ij} = q_i^Ta_j$, $v_j = a_j - \sum r_{ij}q_i$, $r_{jj} = \|v_j\|$ (use the modified version!).
  • Householder: $H = I - \frac{2vv^T}{v^Tv}$, $v = x + \mathrm{sign}(x_1)\|x\|e_1$, $Hx = -\mathrm{sign}(x_1)\|x\|e_1$. Example $x = (2,1,2)$: $v = (5,1,2)$, $Hx = (-3,0,0)$.
  • Givens: $c = a/r$, $s = b/r$, $G = \begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-s&c\end{pmatrix}$, $G(3,4)^T = (5,0)^T$.

3. Practice

  • Householder QR: $2mn^2 - \frac23n^3$ flops, backward stable; normal equations $mn^2 + \frac13n^3$ but the condition is squared.
  • Linearising: $\ln y = \ln a + bt$ for $y = ae^{bt}$; polynomials are linear in the coefficients; weighted variant $A^TWAx = A^TWb$.
  • For rank loss: singular value decomposition, minimal-norm solution $x = A^+b$.

4. Typical Mistakes

  • Normal equations with $AA^T$ instead of $A^TA$.
  • Choice of sign in Householder (cancellation in $v_1$).
  • Classical instead of modified Gram–Schmidt for nearly dependent columns.
